title: Wetherby Halifax Memorial
memorial_details: Memorial on the site of the crash at Wetherby golf course, West Yorkshire. Two engines were excavated from the site in 1978; one is now displayed at the Yorkshire Air Museum.
narrative: Halifax DG226 of 1652 Heavy Conversion Unit departed Marston Moor on 24 August 1944 on a training flight. The port outer engine caught fire at 1000ft; the crew were unable to feather it. The aircraft rolled inverted and dived in. There were no survivors. The engine was recovered at the time; two further engines were excavated in 1978, one of which is now on display at the Yorkshire Air Museum.
cause_of_loss: Engine fire on climb — port outer caught fire at 1000ft, unable to feather; aircraft rolled inverted and crashed
community_connection: Two engines were recovered from the crash site during excavations in 1978. One engine is displayed at the Yorkshire Air Museum.
